answer: For a Sybil cluster, marginal capital cost scales super-linearly as the square of stake share, so attacking 10% of consensus requires 100x collateral, while quadratic slashing erodes committed jade by the square of detected deviation, ensuring each additional thread of stake multiplies loss exposure beyond any extracted walnut of value. Thus, equilibrium security holds when the marginal attack cost, c(n) ~ n², exceeds the maximal extractable rent, R, at n* = sqrt(R/c₀), guaranteeing protocol-level consensus remains economically inviolable.
